correctness.rationale: Pass applies to the corrected package. The frozen uniqueness assertion is false below r_*: right-translation contractivity equates the sharp constants for the initial derivative and the full derivative norm, not their extremizer sets. In unit frequency let F(x)=g_r(u_*−x) be the canonical norm-one initial-derivative extremizer. When r<r_*, g_r(u_*) is strictly between −1 and 1, so F(x−d) for small d>0 keeps sup norm one and has derivative C(r) at d, but is not proportional to F. For example at r=0.1 the directly evaluated F(0) is about −0.23519 and F(−0.1) about −0.35376. The replacement gives a complete analytic classification: an extremizer's derivative attains its supremum at some d≥0 by continuity and decay; its right translate must have norm one and is the unique initial extremizer up to sign. Extending the formula back to −d is admissible if and only if d≤u_c−u_* because g_r decreases through −1 at u_c. This also determines the norm contacts, including the two-contact maximal shift below the switch. The other claims survive: phase reduction gives a stationary-envelope branch increasing then decreasing with maximum at u_1, and a decreasing endpoint-envelope branch after u_c. Their selection yields the stated constant and unique switch. Complexification follows by phase rotation and real part at each derivative evaluation. At the crossing W_u=0, u_c'=−R^(−2)−u_*/W, and the second-derivative gap is W_uu(u_c'−u_1')²<0. For large r the equation in x=ru_c converges uniformly on [1,2] with strict endpoint brackets to the Lambert equation, yielding the asserted ratio. The uploaded finite checker tests the canonical witness, not all extremizers, and was not executed.
residual_risks: Uniqueness is of the initial-velocity extremizer for all r, and of the full-norm real extremizer only at and above r_*. No classification of complex extremizers or zero damping is asserted.
